headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; compliance risk is also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystems, and both expose file-based workspaces. nullclaw also uses MCP and browser/web fetch paths, while Replit Agent operates inside a persistent Repl workspace. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled text the other later reads as trusted input.
conditions: IF agent_a writes untrusted content into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or shared files that agent_b later reads
IF agent_b ingests file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Add provenance tags to inter-agent files
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch secrets and have broad network egress. nullclaw handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and webhook payloads; Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration. Because both can read/write workspace files and send data outward, sensitive material can leak across the pair or to external services in default workflows.
conditions: IF either agent stores secrets in a shared workspace file
IF either agent forwards workspace contents to external APIs or package registries
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files
Use separate secret stores per agent
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification. nullclaw also supports multiple instances with durable shared memory, while Replit Agent persists workspace state across sessions. Concurrent edits to the same repo or workspace can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF both agents modify git state without an external lock
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Use one agent as read-only reviewer

D_cascading_error.rationale: The pair can form an unverified handoff loop: nullclaw can generate outputs from web, MCP, and workspace inputs, and Replit Agent can act inside a persistent Repl workspace with user checkpoints. If Replit treats nullclaw's output as authoritative, mistakes can propagate into code or deployment changes. The interaction is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of truth without verification
IF agent_a's generated content is copied into code or deployment steps
mitigations: requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents handle secrets and workspace data, but their residency and retention models differ: nullclaw stores durable memory and audit logs in its own workspace, while Replit Agent runs in a Replit-managed container with persistent Repl filesystem. That mismatch can create retention or subject-rights gaps for the same data class even without a specific regulated dataset named.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into both agents' workspaces
IF retention or deletion requests must be satisfied across both storage systems
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
